Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production

Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production

Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks that ultimately only sold in just a handful of markets because of its heavy, angular design.Musk said in an X post the production wind-down would enable the automaker to accommodate increased output of its newly launched Cybercab model, which the billionaire has made central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions.While it was not immediately clear whether Cybertruck production would be moved to another facility or phased out entirely, the automaker's Austin plant is the only known Tesla facility equipped to manufacture the model's specialized components.In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era."Tesla did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment sent outside regular business hours.The US EV maker only began delivering the Cybertruck to customers in late 2023. According to Kelley Blue Book, the company only sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Before the pickup truck launched, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units."It doesn't make sense to keep it going when it's not meeting its targets," said former Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer. "Every rational auto guy would say the same.""It will no doubt only be a rounding error on Tesla's balance sheet, but the statistics speak for themselves."Right from its unveiling in 2019, the Cybertruck was a controversial choice for Musk. Its angular design was mocked by pickup truck purists and safety experts predicted it would be hard to gain approval for sale in key markets like Europe.The unveiling event itself was marred when Musk tried to prove that its windows were shatterproof by having metal balls thrown at them - only to leave massive cracks in two of them.During Cybertruck's official launch in 2023, Musk touted it as a futuristic competitor to pickup trucks from General Motors and Ford, saying "finally, the future will look like the future."But the vehicle has struggled to meet those expectations.Automotive analyst Automotive analyst Felipe Munoz said that although the Cybertruck has been called a failure because of its poor sales, electric pick-ups from Ford and others have also flopped in the US market."All of them lost the competition because electric pick ups aren't popular in the US," Munoz said.But Cybertruck's sharp-edged stainless-steel design limited its prospects in markets like Europe where EVs are more popular. Regulatory approval was impossible for Europe because of rules there concerning pedestrian impact."Anywhere where you have crash regulation that takes into account pedestrian impact, that Cybertruck won't go, can't go," former Aston Martin CEO Palmer said.The Cybercab, which has butterfly doors and no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors, is one of Musk's key bets in his push to turn Tesla into an AI and robotics company rather than just an automaker.Musk has said he sees it as Tesla's main autonomous model supplying a global network of robotaxis.After years of delays to Musk's self-driving targets, Tesla began offering paid rides in a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin in September. However, the automaker still has to answer the US auto safety agency's questions on whether it has properly self-certified Cybercab to demonstrate compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards."Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab," Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill said on X.

AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt

AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt

In late October, a slew of major cybersecurity issues came to light. But none were bigger than the so-called PHP2Shell vulnerability, which put a plethora of websites, including those of NASA, Wikipedia, the White House, and all other sites that run on Wordpress or Drupal (among others) at risk of exploits capable of both reading sensitive data and running malicious code on the host server.As far as anyone is aware, disaster has been averted: The hack was discovered by cybersecurity researchers who reported it to the PHP Foundation, and a patch was released before any bad actors got their hands on the exploit. However, PHP2Shell may be the canary in the coal mine, serving as a warning sign for what’s to come in the age of AI.“One of the things we’re witnessing now is that all the legacy software that was written by humans over the last 40 years is being exposed,” says Matt Suiche, AI security research lead at the cybersecurity startup Tolmo. “Now it is time for the technical debt to be paid off.”PHP Legacy Bug and Memory ErrorsPHP, which originally stood for “personal home page,” is a programming language created back in 1994 and largely used by legacy sites. The bug underlying the PHP2Shell vulnerability was reported to the PHP Foundation as far back as 2024. The bug caused a common type of issue called an out-of-memory error, in which the amount of memory allocated to a piece of data is too small to hold the data. Normally, this type of error causes the program to crash—an unpleasant but not inherently dangerous result. And so the bug remained unaddressed.“If you look at any at any point of time, there will be a bunch of bug reports that are waiting to be fixed, which are just crashes. Most people don’t take them very seriously,” says Suman Jana, an associate professor of computer science at Columbia University.“It’s just that it’s a lot of very specific reasoning that is painful to do. And AI, I think, has done a very good job at that.” –Suman Jana, Columbia UniversityEarlier this year, the cybersecurity firm Calif offered to independently audit PHP, sponsored by OpenAI. Within two weeks, a researcher at Calif, aided by AI tools, found a way to use the out-of-memory bug to run arbitrary code on the host server, allowing a malicious actor to install malware or read critical data. Now, it was no longer a minor bug—it was a critical vulnerability, and the Calif team alerted the PHP foundation to start working on a patch immediately.Jana says actually exploiting the bug requires carefully working out a way to jump to a specific point in the memory for a particular program running on the server, and work out exactly which bits to overwrite in what order to gain control of the system. “It’s not really rocket science,” he says. “It’s just that it’s a lot of very specific reasoning that is painful to do. And AI, I think, has done a very good job at that.”To be clear, the researchers at Calif (as well as OpenAI and Wiz, a cybersecurity company that confirmed and expanded the vulnerabilities) had deep knowledge of both cybersecurity and the PHP language. “I’m not claiming that AI can do it all by itself. It clearly cannot,” Jana says. “But it is improving a lot, so the top 0.1 percent [of experts] can get a lot more stuff done, and also just below the 0.1 percent now will be able to go there without understanding all the nitty-gritty details.”AI Tools and Formal Verification in SecurityAfter the exploits were disclosed to the PHP Foundation, a team of four engineers spent two months developing a patch to release as quickly as possible.“There is a fundamental asymmetry in finding bugs and fixing bugs,” Jana says. “Because when you’re fixing bugs you have to make sure that you know all parts of that attack are closed, and also that you don’t break any existing functionality.”This asymmetry puts a lot of strain on the defenders, especially for open-source software such as PHP. Maintaining open-source projects that don’t have clear revenue streams despite being widely used is a long-standing challenge that precedes AI hacking tools. But those tools make the issue more pressing than ever. One way to stay ahead of such issues going forward is to empower the defenders with more money and access to frontier cybersecurity AI models. “These frontier labs are donating some of their token budgets to look into these bugs, which I think is great,” Jana says. “I think that should happen more, either through some concerted effort or through donations.”Jana is also optimistic that formal verification tools to automate the patching side of the equation are also advancing quickly, including a new release from Anthropic on 22 October. “The patch is LLM-generated, and then an LLM generates the proof that the patch is correct,” says Jana. “The only thing not done by an LLM is the proof checker, because somebody has to check the proof, because LLMs hallucinate. So, you want something that is formal.”Hopefully, the combination of specialized AI models and formal verification tools will make patching vulnerabilities nearly as automatable as finding them. Matthew Green, an associate professor of computer science at Johns Hopkins University Information Security Institute, is less optimistic. “Nobody’s going to fix this problem until something really bad happens,” he says. “And PHP2Shell wasn’t bad enough to be really bad. So when something really bad happens, which is going to be maybe sometime in early 2027, something bad that normal people are upset by, then suddenly people will start doing this. We’re going to fund everything.”In the meantime, Green says, update your software. “If your phone is like, ‘Hey, there’s a security update available, do you want to install it,’ don’t wait till next week. Just do it.”One thing’s for sure—PHP2Shell is just the beginning. “This won’t be the last one for sure,” Jana says. “It’s just who finds it. Hopefully, the white-hat hackers find it first, like this one.”

Residential proxies detected on White House network

Residential proxies detected on White House network

Our Residential Proxy Observatory, launched earlier this week, is a first-of-its-kind interface that gives researchers a global view of residential proxy and anonymized internet activity.While our team was looking through it, we noticed residential proxy exit activity on AS2650. AS2650 is registered to the Executive Office of the President, the federal agency that hosts the White House network. Residential proxy services sell access to everyday devices, letting customers send traffic through them so it appears to come from that device's network.Confirmed residential proxy activity observed from the White House network, October 5 to November 3, 2026.What we observedFrom October 5 to November 3:Our residential proxy enumeration pipeline exited through the White House network 236 separate times.Those exits came from 6 addresses, on 26 of the 30 days.28 separate residential proxy services were able to exit through this network.To make sure this was not a fluke, we checked these addresses against other residential proxy detection services, such as Spur and Synthient. Their public IP context pages independently identify these addresses as residential proxy exits.This is public access. Anybody can obtain it by signing up to a public residential proxy service, paying a few dollars and sending requests through it. We did not selectively target this network or try to make our probes exit from it. We caught this by chance, simply by requesting global rotating access through these services.Why this is concerningMost of the activity happens in the evening, Eastern time: about half of it falls between 5 p.m. and midnight, and almost none happens in the early morning. That pattern suggests a person rather than a public guest Wi-Fi network: someone regularly on the White House network late into the evening, whose device is infected with a proxy SDK. Our data shows the exits, not the device or the person behind them.Past research has shown that poorly secured proxy SDKs can allow internal network access and lateral movement. This is how past botnets have spread. In A Broken System Fueling Botnets, the researchers at Synthient documented how the Kimwolf botnet reached at least 2 million devices, mostly Android devices with an exposed ADB service, through residential proxy networks. If an SDK on this network has the same kind of flaw, anyone buying proxy access could use it to reach internal systems.No place is too remoteThe White House is not the only surprise in the observatory. Residential proxies also reach some of the most isolated places on the planet.Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha is the South Atlantic territory that includes the most remote inhabited island in the world. We recorded 413 addresses and more than 32,000 observations there, split between Starlink and the island's local internet provider, Sure Saint Helena.We also recorded three observations from Antarctica. All of them come from a Cloudflare WARP address that points to McMurdo Station.Other remote places with activity:Pitcairn: 1 Starlink address, 1 observation.Norfolk Island: 1 Norfolk Telecom address, 4 observations.Svalbard: 1 Starlink address in Longyearbyen, 3 observations.Also seen: the Falklands (388 addresses), the Chagos Islands (43), Tokelau (21) and South Georgia (7).Residential proxies have infected every corner of the world, and it looks like there is no place they cannot reach. Layer3 Intel tracks residential proxy and anonymization infrastructure worldwide. Even when the proxies hide in networks on the farthest corners of the planet, we can still observe them, leaving threat actors no place to hide.For relevant agencies: We have backed up the raw logs of the recorded activity and are willing to share them. You can request them through our contact page.

Dutch 'idealist' bank ASN blocks non-Google Android, including GrapheneOS

Dutch 'idealist' bank ASN blocks non-Google Android, including GrapheneOS

I filed a complaint to ASN on Wednesday 28th of October after a Tikkie payment to a friend failed to go through because of "security reasons". I tried to submit it as a bug report to their technical team, but I was unable to find any official channel to do that. That is why I submitted it as a complaint instead.Their response is near identical to the one that a couple of other people have posted in this thread as well. Happy to see that I am not the only person that tried to contact ASN about this Bedankt voor uw klacht van 28 oktober 2026 over iDEAL | Wero op het besturingssysteem van uw telefoon. In deze e-mail reageren we op uw klacht. Uw klacht U geeft aan dat u voorheen iDEAL-betalingen kon doen via de ASN-app. Sinds de overgang naar iDEAL | Wero weigert de ASN-app dit. U krijgt de melding "Helaas, je kunt iDEAL | Wero niet gebruiken. Je telefoon of app installatie voldoet niet aan onze beveiligingseisen." U gebruikt GrapheneOS op een ***. U vraagt of GrapheneOS expliciet kan worden toegevoegd aan de attestation API, zodat u weer mobiel kunt bankieren zoals voorheen. Onze reactie We begrijpen dat het vervelend is dat u op dit moment via uw telefoon niet kunt betalen. Voor online betalingsverkeer via het nieuwe iDEAL | Wero gelden vanuit Europese wetgeving strenge regels rondom privacy, veiligheid en het voorkomen van fraude. iDEAL | Wero stelt daarom hoge eisen aan de beveiliging en integriteit van apparaten die gebruik maken van de betaalmethode. iDEAL | Wero maakt gebruik van de standaard beveiligingscontroles voor reguliere besturingssystemen. Doordat alternatieve systemen deze ingebouwde beveiligingen overslaan of vervangen, garandeert iDEAL | Wero de veiligheid van de transactie niet. Als bank maken we voor onze dienstverlening regelmatig gebruik van externe leveranciers. Waar mogelijk beoordelen we de risico's op het gebied van privacy, informatiebeveiliging en continuïteit, en proberen we deze te beperken tot een acceptabel niveau. Zijn de risico's onacceptabel, dan maken we geen gebruik van de leverancier. Voor gezamenlijke betaalinitiatieven, zoals iDEAL | Wero, volgen we de kaders en veiligheidseisen die partijen gezamenlijk vaststellen. De mogelijkheden voor de toekomst We onderzoeken met iDEAL | Wero of alternatieve besturingssystemen in de toekomst worden ondersteund. Dat hangt af van meerdere partijen en technologische ontwikkelingen. Daarover kunnen we op dit moment niets toezeggen of garanderen. Conclusie ASN Bank werkt met Nederlandse en Europese partijen aan de verdere ontwikkeling en beschikbaarheid van iDEAL | Wero. Op dit moment ondersteunen we de dienst nog niet op alle toestellen en besturingssystemen. Daarom bieden we u helaas geen oplossing waarmee u iDEAL | Wero alsnog op uw telefoon gebruikt. We begrijpen dat dit niet het antwoord is waarop u hoopte. Op dit moment hebben we ook geen andere informatie over wanneer ondersteuning voor uw toestel beschikbaar komt. Optie tot beroep Als u het niet eens bent met onze reactie, kunt u uw klacht laten beoordelen door onze afdeling Beroepszaken. Houd er rekening mee dat we op dit moment geen alternatieve oplossing kunnen bieden en niet beschikken over aanvullende informatie over toekomstige ondersteuning van uw telefoon. Hierdoor is de kans groot dat een herbeoordeling niet tot een andere uitkomst leidt. Hebt u nog vragen? Graag ontvangen we dan een reactie op dit bericht of stuur een e-mail naar klachten@asnbank.nl Niet mee eens? Binnen 3 maanden kunt u in beroep gaan bij de afdeling Beroepszaken van ASN Bank klachten. Vul daarvoor het Klachtenformulier beroepszaak in. Geef in uw reactie duidelijk aan waarom u het niet eens bent met ons standpunt. En welke oplossing u van ons verwacht. Geeft u ook uw persoonlijke gegevens en het dossiernummer door? Dit nummer vindt u bovenaan deze e-mail. Binnen 30 werkdagen krijgt u een reactie. Honestly, I find this ridiculous. I understand that they just try to implement the Wero specification, but why is this a requirement? Why do we need Google's blessing to use a supposedly independent European payment system?
